{"paper":"LS11",
 "part0_abstract_claims":[
  "After subtraction of the model, the residuals showed an approximate linear upward trend after 1942.",
  "The resulting full natural plus anthropogenic model fits the entire 160 year record very well.",
  "Residual analysis does not provide any evidence for a substantial cooling effect due to sulfate aerosols from 1940 to 1970.",
  "The cooling observed during that period may be due to a natural 60-year cycle",
  "New solar activity proxy models are developed that suggest a mechanism for both the 60-year climate cycle and a portion of the long-term warming trend.",
  "Our results suggest that ... the anthropogenic contribution to climate change since 1970 should be around half of that previously claimed by the IPCC [2007].",
  "A 21st Century forecast suggests that climate may warm less than 1 \u00baC by 2100."],
 "claims":[

  "E1":"States IPCC AR4 fig 9.5a/b position (>90% anthropogenic) and argues against it (p19)",
  "E1b":"Load-bearing rebuttal citation is self-citation '[Scafetta, 2010]' (p19)",
  "P1a":"Cycles fit to pre-1950 data, extrapolated forward (p6; executed p8)",
  "P1b":"Headline attribution split and 2100 forecast rest on in-sample fit (p8, p15)",
  "P2a":"Table 1 gives parameter standard errors; residual slope 0.66+/-0.08 (SI p29; p8)",

  "P6":"Cycle mechanisms 'not understood yet'; only speculation offered (p5)",
  "P7":"No autocorrelation/effective-df correction; SI noise test uses fitted model as null (p8, SI p38)"}}
